 Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million cars over airbag safety risk
 Defective Takata inflators have previously caused at least 28 deaths and more than 400 injuries in the United States since 2009
 David Shepardson Saturday 21 November 2026 05:03 EST

 Honda and Toyota Motor announced on Friday that they are recalling around 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs due to potential rupture risks with Takata airbag inflators.
 Both manufacturers stated that no crashes, injuries or inflator ruptures have been linked to the affected vehicles. The carmakers plan to fit replacement airbag inflators across all the recalled models.
 Defective Takata inflators have previously caused at least 28 deaths and more than 400 injuries in the United States since 2009, sparking the largest safety recall in US automotive history. At least 20 of those fatal accidents occurred in Honda cars, and all prior deaths involved inflators that lacked a drying agent.
 By contrast, the inflators fitted in this latest batch of recalled vehicles contain moisture-absorbing material.
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration noted that analysis and degradation simulation models carried out by independent test groups enabled the manufacturers to act before any safety risks materialised.
 "Honda and Toyota saw early evidence of degradation risk in certain of their vehicles and are currently conducting proactive recalls ‌of vehicles," NHTSA said late Friday, adding that other automakers continue ‌to conduct inflator analysis and testing.
 open image in gallery A technician holds an earlier recalled Takata airbag inflator in Miami, Florida on June 25, 2015. REUTERS/Joe Skipper/File Photo ( Reuters ) The recall includes 810,592 older Honda cars and SUVs in the United States and 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the United States.
 The Toyota recall includes 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 IS250, 2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 ⁠Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner. The Honda recall covers some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles.
 The Honda recall covers vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperature, humidity and large temperature fluctuations.
 Over the past decade, two dozen major automakers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide, including about 67 million vehicles in the United States.
 Various automakers have also reported hundreds of injuries in vehicles since ‌2009 from Takata airbag inflators that can explode, unleashing metal shrapnel inside cars and trucks, killing ​or injuring drivers or other vehicle occupants.
 Honda said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential ‌propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions.
 Toyota ⁠warned that degraded propellant could cause the inflator to rupture if the airbag deploys ⁠and cause serious injuries.
 The Honda recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto ‌Rico, US Virgin Islands, Northern ​Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa.
 Toyota did not specify in ‌which US states the recall applies but said ​it expects the replacement inflators will be ready by early 2027.
